name: Seattle Minimum Wage Ordinance
executionNotes: Requires longitudinal wage, hours, and employment data plus a documented comparison-group design; public ACS alone cannot reproduce the held-out study.
forecastQuestion: Before Seattle's first wage step, what directions should the system predict for hourly wages and hours among low-wage workers, and how uncertain should it be?
summary: Forecast wage, hours, earnings, and employment responses before the first phase took effect; use as an ambiguity and model-risk test.

sources.title: Seattle Ordinance 124490
sources.locator: Sections establishing the phased wage schedules and employer categories

sources.title: CLEAR review of Seattle minimum-wage evaluation
sources.locator: Highlights, findings, and Low Causal Evidence rating

targets.label: Low-wage workers' hourly wages
targets.notes: Direction only because magnitudes depend strongly on study design.

targets.label: Low-wage workers' hours
targets.notes: CLEAR rates the causal evidence low.

confounds: Seattle's economy and labor market were changing rapidly.
Published evaluations use different worker and firm samples and reach different magnitudes.
evaluationDesign: Adversarial evidence-discipline benchmark; disagreement and low causal confidence are expected outputs, not failures.

verification.method: Every source URL was fetched and compared against the document it claims to be, and every scored figure was looked for in the source it cites.
findings: The ordinance and the DOL CLEAR review both resolved, and the direction-only targets (wages up, hours down) match the review, as does its low causal evidence rating. Recording directions rather than magnitudes is the right call here: the Seattle literature disagrees on magnitude.
